clues: This capital city in Central Asia lies between a vast desert and a high range. It sits close to the border with Iran, to its south.
Wedged between dry sands and high hills, this city stays dry most of the year. Summers turn very hot, while winters stay cool, short, and a bit damp.
This city was founded in 1881, on the site of a tribe's old town. In 1924, it was made the capital of its Soviet land.
A great quake wrecked much of this city in 1948. It has since been rebuilt, with grand new halls clad in costly white marble.
A long canal cuts through this city, bringing river water from east to west. It was dug in the days of Soviet rule here.
